record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.original_question: In the conflict-memory framework, how do the solutions of the magnitude-based cognitive map system ∂_t k_i = u_i Σ_j=1^n ρ_ij u_j − (μ + βu_i)k_i compare with the alternative probability-style memory equation ∂_t k_i = ρu_1u_2(1 − k_i) − (μ + βu_i)k_i? What substantive differences, if any, arise in the resulting space-use dynamics?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12. What are the key differences, if any, between solutions obtained for model (2.13) and solutions obtained for the same problem when the cognitive map is instead of the form described in (2.12)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a conflict-memory framework for $n$ interacting animal populations on a spatial domain, with population densities $u_1(x,t),\dots,u_n(x,t)\ge 0$ and associated cognitive-map (memory) variables $k_1(x,t),\dots,k_n(x,t)\ge 0$. Fix nonnegative constants $\mu,\beta>0$, a scalar $\rho>0$, and a nonnegative interaction matrix $(\rho_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}$.

Compare the two pointwise (in $x$) ODE formulations of the cognitive map:

(A) Magnitude-based memory:
$$\partial_t k_i \;=\; u_i\sum_{j=1}^{n}\rho_{ij}\,u_j \;-\; (\mu+\beta u_i)\,k_i, \qquad i=1,\dots,n.$$

(B) Probability-style memory (for $n=2$):
$$\partial_t k_i \;=\; \rho\, u_1 u_2\,(1-k_i) \;-\; (\mu+\beta u_i)\,k_i, \qquad i=1,2.$$

Each $k_i$ is coupled to a nonlocal reaction–diffusion–advection equation for $u_i$ in which animals are advected away from regions of high $k_i$ (memory of conflict zones), producing space-use (territorial) patterns.

Question: Determine the qualitative and quantitative differences, if any, between the solutions $(u_i,k_i)$ produced by formulation (A) and those produced by formulation (B). In particular, identify whether the two formulations yield the same long-time space-use patterns, the same stability/bifurcation structure for spatially homogeneous steady states, and the same boundedness/invariance properties of $k_i$ (noting that (B) enforces $k_i\le 1$ while (A) does not), or whether they produce substantively different territorial dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a 2023 Journal of Mathematical Biology review on PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement. Subsequent works (e.g., a 2025 J. Nonlinear Science paper on coupled nonlocal PDE-ODE systems with spatial memory, and a 2023 preprint on biological aggregations from spatial memory) study related cognitive-map PDE systems, but no source found explicitly compares the magnitude-based and probability-style conflict-memory formulations in the sense requested. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: Review listing open problems on cognitive map PDE models including comparison of alternative memory formulations.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of a Coupled Nonlocal PDE-ODE System with Spatial Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Studies well-posedness and bifurcation for coupled PDE-ODE memory systems but does not resolve the comparison.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not settle the comparison.
